reports.title: Emerson Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2026 Results;

guidance.heading: 2027 Outlook
section: The following tables summarize the fiscal year 2027 guidance framework, which assumes returning ~$3.8B through ~$2.5B of share repurchases and ~$1.3B of dividends.

Guidance figures are approximate. | 2027 Q1 | 2027
Net Sales Growth | ~5% | ~5%
Underlying Sales Growth | ~5% | ~5%
Earnings Per Share | $1.19 - $1.23 | ~$5.70
Amortization of intangibles | ~$0.35 | ~$1.41
Restructuring and related costs | ~$0.04 | ~$0.14
Adjusted Earnings Per Share | $1.58 - $1.62 | ~$7.25
Operating Cash Flow | $4.3B - $4.4B
Free Cash Flow | $3.8B - $3.9B
Share Repurchase | ~$1.5B | ~$2.5B

desk.headline: Sales up 7% to $5.2bn, adjusted EPS $1.86 just ahead of estimates; first fiscal 2027 outlook sees about $7.25 adjusted EPS
results: Fourth-quarter sales rose 7% (also 7% underlying) to $5.2bn; adjusted EPS rose 15% to $1.86 against a $1.85 estimate, and GAAP EPS rose 24% to $1.33.
Underlying orders grew 14%; the Software & Systems group led with sales up 14%, while Intelligent Devices grew 5% and Safety & Productivity 2%.
Adjusted segment EBITA margin widened 160 bps to 29.1%; the Software & Systems margin reached 32.3%.
Full fiscal 2026: sales $18.98bn (+5%), adjusted EPS $6.59 (+10%), free cash flow $3.5bn (+9%); $1.0bn spent on buybacks.
Quarterly dividend raised 7% to $0.595 a share.

guidance.summary: First outlook for fiscal 2027: about 5% sales growth, adjusted EPS of about $7.25 (about $5.70 GAAP) and $3.8–3.9bn of free cash flow, with about $3.8bn returned to shareholders ($2.5bn buybacks, $1.3bn dividends). Q1 adjusted EPS is guided at $1.58–1.62.

points: Orders were strong across the board: power-related business up about 25%, LNG sales up 68% and semiconductor orders up 59%; China and Europe remain weak.
Backlog reached $8.2bn (+11%) and the project pipeline about $13bn (+17%), with more long-cycle work now in the order book.
Middle East orders rose 42%; the 2027 plan assumes high-single-digit growth there if the conflict does not escalate.
The plan builds in about 2% price; tariffs should be slightly better than this year, but memory-chip costs are a headwind.
About $1.5bn of the $2.5bn buyback is planned for Q1; management is looking at bolt-on deals but no large acquisition.
call.source: Call transcript: The Motley Fool, 4 Nov 2026; consensus revenue from Investing.com, 4 Nov 2026

watch: Whether Q1 adjusted EPS lands in the $1.58–1.62 range, with margin guided lower at about 28%.
Conversion of the $8.2bn backlog as more long-cycle orders stretch delivery times.
Middle East conflict and weak China and Europe demand versus the 5% growth plan.
